curated_families.signature: dma_copy requires src and dst to have the same number of elements, got src=N, dst=N
curated_families.cause: the destination tile does not hold exactly the elements of the source slice (a cache sized by a tile where the full-width chunk is required)
curated_families.fix: size the cache by k_tiles * W (the operand's full width) and copy full-width chunks; operand views then slide inside that cache

curated_families.signature: dma_copy <dst|src> partition dimension N exceeds maximum M
curated_families.cause: one tile was allocated for more rows than the partition axis allows (max 128)
curated_families.fix: loop over the partition dimension in <=128-row chunks, allocate the tile per chunk; never pad a smaller dimension up to 128

curated_families.signature: Out-of-bound access ... index range [a, b] exceeds dimension size N
curated_families.cause: a bound or slice end was computed past the tensor's extent
curated_families.fix: derive bounds from the tensor's own shape; the final chunk may be partial; partition <= 128

curated_families.signature: Matmul contraction dimension N exceeds pmax=M
curated_families.cause: one nc_matmul was given a K chunk larger than the hardware contraction limit
curated_families.fix: split K into pmax-sized chunks and accumulate all chunks into ONE psum tile

curated_families.signature: Matmul stationary free dimension N exceeds gemm_stationary_fmax=M
curated_families.cause: the stationary operand slice is wider than the stationary free limit (128); typical overshoot: slicing the full operand width instead of a TILE_M window
curated_families.fix: slice the stationary operand in TILE_M-wide windows (<=128); keep K on the partition axis

curated_families.signature: <op> must be in ['sbuf', 'psum'], got shared_hbm
curated_families.cause: an on-chip operation was pointed at HBM
curated_families.fix: dma_copy is the only HBM bridge; go psum -> sbuf with tensor_copy, then dma_copy sbuf -> shared_hbm

curated_families.signature: <op> must be in ['psum'], got <region> / must be in ['sbuf'], got <region>
curated_families.cause: a tile sits in the wrong memory region for its operation
curated_families.fix: nc_matmul: dst in nl.psum, stationary and moving in nl.sbuf; move tiles with tensor_copy

curated_families.signature: value array of shape (N, N) could not be broadcast to indexing result of shape (N, N)
curated_families.cause: an assignment wrote a value whose shape differs from the destination slice
curated_families.fix: match both sides exactly; nothing broadcasts or reshapes

curated_families.signature: module 'nki.language' has no attribute 'X'
curated_families.cause: the model invented an API name (nl.value, nl.scalar, nl.dot, tile.mean)
curated_families.fix: use only real names: nl.ndarray, nl.affine_range, nl.sum(view, axis=[...]), nisa.dma_copy, nisa.nc_matmul, nisa.tensor_copy, nisa.tensor_scalar, tile.ap

curated_families.signature: 'X' object has no attribute 'Y'
curated_families.cause: a numpy-ism was applied to a tile
curated_families.fix: use nl/nisa operations instead of numpy attributes

curated_families.signature: got multiple values for argument
curated_families.cause: one argument was passed twice (positionally and by keyword)
curated_families.fix: pass every argument exactly once, by keyword

curated_families.signature: must have at least 2 dimensions
curated_families.cause: a 1-D tile was allocated
curated_families.fix: every tile is (rows, cols); a length-N vector is (1, N) or (N, 1)

curated_families.signature: cannot reshape array of size
curated_families.cause: the kernel attempted a reshape
curated_families.fix: do not reshape; slice the given shapes into tiles

curated_families.signature: 'MemoryRegion' object is not callable
curated_families.cause: nl.sbuf / nl.psum / nl.shared_hbm were called like functions
curated_families.fix: pass the region as buffer= to nl.ndarray

curated_families.signature: unsupported operand type(s) for <op>: 'NkiTensor' and ...
curated_families.cause: a python operator was used on a tile
curated_families.fix: accumulate in a psum tile via nc_matmul, or use nisa ops

curated_families.signature: NUMERICAL MISMATCH: worst error X of the output's RMS (Y), tolerance Z
curated_families.cause: the kernel runs but computes wrong numbers
curated_families.fix: run the behavioral diagnosis: stationary operand stuck / only one k-chunk / dtype or layout fault; apply the matching menu guidance

curated_families.signature: CORRECT, BUT TOO MUCH HBM TRAFFIC FOR THIS LEVEL
curated_families.cause: the numbers are right but the kernel moves more bytes than the level gate allows (1.60x / 1.25x / 1.05x)
curated_families.fix: find the operand still re-read per outer-loop pass and give it the cached treatment (stack_stationary_operand / stack_moving_operand_symmetrically)

curated_families.signature: TRAFFIC UNMEASURED / bytes below the byte floor
curated_families.cause: the measurement is incomplete, or the kernel moves fewer bytes than any correct kernel can (it skips required reads -- the computation is broken)
curated_families.fix: fail closed: restore the full computation, then re-measure; never accept a below-floor count

curated_families.signature: THE KERNEL MODIFIED ITS INPUT (argument N)
curated_families.cause: the kernel wrote into one of its input tensors
curated_families.fix: allocate a new output with buffer=nl.shared_hbm and return that

curated_families.signature: CORRECT ON CPU BUT WRONG ON HARDWARE: <simulator warning>
curated_families.cause: the simulator flagged a pattern that is numerically correct on CPU and incorrect on the device
curated_families.fix: restructure the flagged pattern (most often the accumulation/psum scheme)

curated_families.signature: RULE VIOLATIONS (banned framework call / entry point missing / @nki.jit missing)
curated_families.cause: a level rule was broken; this scores zero however fast the kernel is
curated_families.fix: remove the framework call (matmul/dot/einsum/@/.T), define the level's entry point, keep it decorated with @nki.jit

curated_families.signature: the file imports but <entry> could not be loaded / defines no `<entry>`
curated_families.cause: the kernel does not define the entry name this level checks through
curated_families.fix: keep the level's entry-point name exactly as the checker expects it
